note: the room at the Swan, asked with no Coin

26.label: Beadle Kempe
26.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Known: Doors open for them. A canvass turns up one more person.

30.label: Informer: Whistle
30.desc: Regina Bader, known in the taverns as Whistle. Works The Market. Meet them on the Ward with Coin for a word.

50.label: Fire at the Tanner Print-shop
50.desc: The fire at the Tanner Print-shop the night before the inspection destroyed exactly what somebody needed destroyed: the stock had been carted out the week before. Everything else survived. Including, in a drawer nobody checked, a bill of lading. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name. (The Abbey Close)

51.label: Dorcas Kürschner
51.desc: Dorcas Kürschner, a tenant put out. Has had a key to the house for years. (Accused in: Fire at the Tanner Print-shop)

53.label: A Word in the Right Ear
53.desc: An informer trusts you now, which in this city is rarer than gold. They tell you which tapster to buy, and which to be seen buying. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Instinct, for good. With your Instinct beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Informers bring word sooner.)

59.label: No Forced Entry
59.desc: Not a mark on the locks. Whoever came in had a key, or was let in by someone who trusted them.

62.label: Nan Haller
62.desc: Nan Haller, a known fire-setter. Chews cloves against the toothache, constantly. (Accused in: Fire at the Tanner Print-shop)

64.label: The Scene Drawn
64.desc: Forty leaves of the Tanner Print-shop in charcoal, numbered and dated. The room as it was.

66.label: Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row
66.desc: The bucket-chain got to a Tenement in Ebner Row in time to save the walls, during the bear-baiting, when the streets were empty. The fire-warden says it started in three places at once. Fires do not do that. A witness saw a cart leaving without a lantern. In the strongbox, unburnt: a bond pledging the building for three times its worth. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name. (The Market)

68.label: Partial: The Columns
68.desc: Without the Apothecary's Key, you only get part of it. The apothecary recovers the columns. They do not add up, and somebody knew they would not.

70.label: Rumour from Whistle
70.desc: Whistle heard something about Fire at the Tanner Print-shop: "They didn't knock. They let themselves in."

74.label: Gregory Bicker
74.desc: Gregory Bicker, the building's owner. Owes a great deal to a moneylender in the Stews. (Accused in: Fire at the Tanner Print-shop)

78.label: The Scene Drawn
78.desc: Forty leaves of a Tenement in Ebner Row in charcoal, numbered and dated. The room as it was.

79.label: The Confessor's Glance
79.desc: A priest looked at a door and would not say why. You know why.

80.label: Partial: The Oil Named
80.desc: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Rape-oil cut with spirit, a blend sold by one chandler in the Abbey Close.

82.label: Warning: Coining
82.desc: Whistle says something is going to happen in The Market: coining. Keep this on the table. When the case comes in you will be ahead of it.

83.label: A Curved Scratch
83.desc: A fresh curved scratch in the wax of the table, the kind a heavy signet leaves on a clenched fist.

84.label: Three Seats of Fire
84.desc: Three places, lit within a minute of each other. One person moving fast, or two moving slowly.

86.label: Apollonia Kempe
86.desc: Apollonia Kempe, a tenant put out. Never takes off a heavy gold signet. (Accused in: Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row)

91.label: The Old Examiner's Method
91.desc: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. Nobody did. But in the drawer of your desk is a leaf in the last examiner's hand, and reading it now, you understand it. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Wit, for good. With your Wit beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Witnesses keep half again as long before they forget.)

100.label: The Council's Letter: Sworn Examiner
100.desc: A magistrate will seal a Writ for you (an Accused with cause, in Explore), and the Council sends you more. Attend on the Council.

103.label: Partial: The Oil Named
103.desc: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Rape-oil cut with spirit, a blend sold by one chandler in the Abbey Close.

items.label: The Getaway

journal.title: A Room at the Swan
journal.text: The landlord of the Swan, who owes the Watch a kindness, offers a room with a fire and a door that locks. One night. Tonight. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Stress
journal.text: You wake at the same hour every night with the same case behind your eyes. You have started to snap at the sergeant. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: Week 6
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Ottilie Kress has taken up one of your cases. The ledger: 1 conviction; 2 open; 10 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Rival Takes a Case
journal.text: Ottilie Kress is working Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row from the other side, with the Harbourmaster's men. Answer it first, or they will.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Rape-oil cut with spirit, a blend sold by one chandler in the Abbey Close.

journal.title: Pardon: Els Bader
journal.text: Els Bader walks out of the Hole into the Market and does not look back. A year from now they keep a stall in the Abbey Close, and a family, and they cross the street when they see you.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: The Council Takes Notice
journal.text: A letter on heavy paper under the city's seal: the Council will see you about the office of Sworn Examiner. Attend on them, in a clean collar.

journal.title: Guilty: Els Bader
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Els Bader is convicted of Burglary at Welser's Pawnshop, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached. At the court door Hal Chandler presses a coin into your hand and will not take it back. An honest fee.

journal.title: Condemned: Els Bader
journal.text: Els Bader goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, A Fine, Pillory, Banished, Branded, The Rope. The Council will follow your word, or its custom. Pleas arrive with the morning: The Guild's Plea.

journal.title: An Insight: The Old Examiner's Method
journal.text: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. Nobody did. But in the drawer of your desk is a leaf in the last examiner's hand, and reading it now, you understand it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at a Tenement in Ebner Row. You find: A Curved Scratch, Three Seats of Fire, The Smell Under the Smoke. The first name in the casebook: Apollonia Kempe.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Coining," says Whistle, "in The Market. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Rape-oil cut with spirit, a blend sold by one chandler in the Abbey Close. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: The Informer's Brother: Send the Watch as planned
journal.text: The brother is taken. Your informer stops meeting your eye. (Standing rises; Vendetta)

journal.title: The Informer's Brother
journal.text: Your informer asks a favour, the first they have ever asked. Their brother runs untaxed wine through the Water-gate. The Watch is due there on Thursday. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: The Confessor: Ask him to point
journal.text: He does not say a word. He looks, once, at a door, and goes back inside to pray for both of you. (A token that names a name; the Bishop frowns)

journal.title: The Confessor
journal.text: A priest of the parish asks for a word. Someone told him something under the seal, and it is eating him. He will not break the seal. He might point. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with a Tenement in Ebner Row before anyone can tidy it. Whatever you find there next will be on record.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Cleared: Barbel Stromer
journal.text: Barbel Stromer has an answer, and it is a good one: a wedding, and forty guests who remember the dancing. They are cleared.

journal.title: Week 5
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The Harbourmaster has sent an examiner of his own. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 7 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Harbourmaster's Examiner
journal.text: Ottilie Kress has the Harbourmaster's letter and a desk in the Customs House. The Harbourmaster wants the Council to see it has a choice. They will work your cases from the other side: close them first, spoil your scenes, pay your witnesses to forget. Question them, buy them, frighten them, or shadow them; find their weakness twice and the Council sends them home.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over the Tanner Print-shop. You find: The Smell Under the Smoke. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Gregory Bicker. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Taken: Els Bader
journal.text: The sergeants take them at the Red Ox, mid-sentence. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: A Word from Whistle
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Fire at the Tanner Print-shop. Whistle does not sign things.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Apothecary's Key, you only get part of it. The apothecary recovers the columns. They do not add up, and somebody knew they would not. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: New Case: Fire at a Tenement in Ebner Row
journal.text: The bucket-chain got to a Tenement in Ebner Row in time to save the walls, during the bear-baiting, when the streets were empty. The fire-warden says it started in three places at once. Fires do not do that. A witness saw a cart leaving without a lantern. In the strongbox, unburnt: a bond pledging the building for three times its worth. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name.

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with the Tanner Print-shop before anyone can tidy it. 2 things you found there will keep now.

journal.title: Corroborated Account
journal.text: The body of the thing and the words of the witnesses finally agree. They point the same way. It was Els Bader, the night porter. It has to be.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Tanner Print-shop. You find: No Forced Entry, A bill of lading, Convenient Losses. The first name in the casebook: Nan Haller. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Week 4
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 7 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: the Tiler talks for an hour. Most of it is about their late husband. Then, almost as an afterthought: "They were rolling a die over their knuckles."

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book: Buy the page
journal.text: A page in a bad hand, with a name on it that you were going to have to find the hard way. (A token that names a name)

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book
journal.text: A pawnbroker keeps a book of everything that came through his door this week, and who brought it. Something from your case is in it. He would part with the page. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. A great deal of it. The barber-surgeon in the Abbey Close stitched a hand the same morning. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: Ahead of the Crier
journal.text: "Something is going to happen," says Whistle. "Soon." Keep the warning on the table: when it comes, you will be ready for it.

journal.title: An Insight: A Word in the Right Ear
journal.text: An informer trusts you now, which in this city is rarer than gold. They tell you which tapster to buy, and which to be seen buying. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: New Case: Fire at the Tanner Print-shop
journal.text: The fire at the Tanner Print-shop the night before the inspection destroyed exactly what somebody needed destroyed: the stock had been carted out the week before. Everything else survived. Including, in a drawer nobody checked, a bill of lading. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Welser's Pawnshop. You find: Blood on the Glass.  The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Pocketed
journal.text: Three weeks' stipend in worn silver. It sits in your coat like a stone. Somewhere, somebody writes your name in a ledger.

journal.title: Week 3
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 6 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Welser's Pawnshop. You find: The Getaway. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Els Bader.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: The round hears things: a word about Burglary at Welser's Pawnshop.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Fire," says Whistle, "in The Abbey Close. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: The Beggar at the Door: Give her a Coin
journal.text: The child gets bread. She tells you who came and went, and the clerks get a story about you. (The Crowd and Dread ease; her word on the case)

journal.title: The Beggar at the Door
journal.text: A woman with a child on her hip has been at the Watch-house door since prime. She does not ask for anything. She just stands there, where the Council's clerks can see her, and she has seen everyone who passed. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Welser's Pawnshop. You find: A Loaded Die, Disturbed Dust. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Matthes Fletcher. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan: Watch who leaves
journal.text: You let it burn out and watch the door. The potboy sees you watching, and sees a living in it. (An Informer at the Swan)

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan
journal.text: The round passes the Swan as two carters go through its window. The tapster is shouting your name. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Pocketed
journal.text: Three weeks' stipend in worn silver. It sits in your coat like a stone. Somewhere, somebody writes your name in a ledger.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Dorcas Kempe takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: Week 2
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: Two drunks, a stolen goose and a lost dog. The dog was the most reasonable of them. Your feet ache all the way up to your skull.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Welser's Pawnshop. The back shutter has been forced with something flat and patient, and the strongbox stands open like a mouth. You come away with The Pried Shutter, The Inventory. A name for the casebook: Hodge Imhoff. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: The Tiler's Word: A Coin for his trouble
journal.text: He saw a face, and he will say so again where it counts. (A Witness who saw it)

journal.title: The Tiler's Word
journal.text: A tiler was on his ladder across the lane when it happened, mending a roof that did not need mending. He says so to anyone with a coin, and now he is saying it to you. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with Welser's Pawnshop before anyone can tidy it. Whatever you find there next will be on record.

journal.title: The Desk Under the Stair
journal.text: The desk is yours now: the tallow stub, the cracked inkhorn, the case already waiting on it. The last examiner to sit here left in a hurry. The city did not stop to notice.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at Welser's Pawnshop
journal.text: Splinters everywhere at Hal Chandler's. Someone went through the shutter, with a crow at the dead of the night, took whatever stood in the shop front, and was gone before the watchman finished shouting. A neighbour reports seeing somebody laughing.

choice.title: A Room at the Swan
choice.text: The landlord of the Swan, who owes the Watch a kindness, offers a room with a fire and a door that locks. One night. Tonight.

options.label: Take the room
options.text: You sleep like the dead and wake like the living.

options.label: Work through
options.text: A Coin for the night's writing, and the ache goes a little deeper.

options.label: Sleep at the desk
options.text: The fire goes out in the Watch-house and you sleep sitting up. The Swan keeps its room.
